summary: Iteration 22 — Password Reset flow + Nightly Cleanup Job verified end-to-end. Backend: 12/12 pytest cases pass (forgot-password enum-guard for registered/unregistered/malformed identifiers, 1-hour token TTL, prior-token invalidation, rate-limit 5/10min observed, reset-password invalid/used/expired/short-password 400s, valid reset updates password_hash + marks token used=true + issues session cookie auto-login + strips password_hash from response, login regression with new password succeeds and old password rejected, /auth/me strips password_hash, and Scheduler startup log confirms both 'digest 08:00 IST' and 'cleanup 03:00 IST' registered). Frontend: All required data-testids present. Login page shows link-forgot-password → navigates to /forgot-password; submitting valid email transitions to forgot-sent state and forgot-dev-hint banner appears with the correct 'Delivery: dev mode' copy. /reset-password without ?token= shows reset-missing-token (form hidden). /reset-password?token=xxx renders reset-form; password mismatch shows inline reset-error without submitting; fake token surfaces server 400 'Invalid or expired reset link.' Real-token E2E: form submit with a Mongo-issued token redirected user to /dashboard, session_token cookie set, 97 credits visible confirming auto-login. Password restored to secret123 post-test.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew to 2475 lines (up from 2313 in iter21, ~2145 in iter20). The >700-line-per-file guideline is now materially violated 3.5x. auth routes, project routes, character routes, TTS pipeline, digest+cleanup schedulers, and billing all live in one file. Extraction into modules (auth.py, projects.py, characters.py, schedulers.py) is overdue and will pay off in every subsequent iteration.

/api/auth/forgot-password rate-limit uses IP-only bucketing. In shared-NAT / mobile-carrier scenarios (e.g., corporate WiFi, Airtel/Jio) this can lock out an entire subnet of legitimate users after 5 requests in 10 min. Consider (identifier + IP) composite key OR raise limit to 10-15 and add per-identifier caps.

_cleanup_job orphan-file check (server.py:2427) does `await db.projects.find_one(...)` inside a tight loop over the characters directory — for a directory with 10k+ portrait files this is 10k sequential DB round-trips. Batch it: read all filenames first, then do ONE `db.projects.find({id:{$in:pids}},{id:1})` and use a set diff. Not a P0 today because dir is small, but the pattern will bite at scale.

_cleanup_job deletion criteria for draft projects uses `$or: [{scenes:{$size:0}}, {scenes:{$exists:false}}]`. This is correct, but if a user genuinely intended a draft with 0 scenes as a WIP >24h, it gets nuked. Consider requiring status='draft' AND created_at<cutoff AND (last touched >24h AND scenes empty). Currently `updated_at` isn't consulted at all.

/api/auth/forgot-password does not lock the mobile-only path: if user has mobile-only account, delivery silently returns 'logged' with no token created (correct behaviour). But the /forgot-password UI never surfaces this — users can enter a mobile-format identifier, the input field has type='email' so browser validation rejects it. UX: either accept mobile numbers OR clearly label the field 'Email address only' (current copy 'SMS-based reset for mobile-only accounts is coming soon.' is subtle — good enough for MVP).

reset_password endpoint does NOT invalidate other active sessions when password is changed (server.py:610-621). If an attacker had a valid session_token when the user resets password, that stolen session remains valid. Recommend: `await db.user_sessions.delete_many({'user_id': rec['user_id']})` before `_issue_session`.

Positive: `password_hash` is correctly stripped from /auth/me, /auth/register, and /auth/reset-password responses (verified in tests). Email-enum guard implementation is genuinely constant-time from an API-surface perspective — malformed / non-existent / registered identifiers all return the same shape. The scheduler adds cleanup_job idempotently via `replace_existing=True` — safe on hot reload.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Rate limit warning: /api/auth/forgot-password is 5/10min per IP. After running the full test_iter22 suite you WILL hit 429 in subsequent runs — restart backend (`sudo supervisorctl restart backend`) to reset the in-memory bucket, as noted in the review request. The auto-login redirect from /reset-password goes to /dashboard (not /). /auth/me returns the user object directly (NOT wrapped in {'user':...}) — this differs from /auth/login and /auth/reset-password which DO wrap in {'user':...}. To E2E the reset flow programmatically, insert a token directly into db.password_reset_tokens (see _mint_token helper in the test file) — safer than depending on forgot-password to succeed under rate limits. Scheduler is confirmed running via backend startup log line 'Schedulers started — digest 08:00 IST + cleanup 03:00 IST daily'.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. All 15 review-request checkpoints passed on the first meaningful run. The two initial test failures were test-side bugs (parallel-execution race on shared user's tokens + /auth/me response shape assumption), both fixed by (a) reordering the rate-limit test to run last and (b) using .get('user', body) for the /auth/me shape. Backend restart between backend+frontend phases is REQUIRED to reset the in-memory rate limiter.
